steps.say: Systemic sclerosis splits by how far skin thickening spreads. Distal only is limited while proximal spread is diffuse. Antibodies are the predictors of the organs at risk. This figure shows the clinical and capillary features that separate the two.
steps.tx: Systemic sclerosis (**SSc**, fibrosing skin and organ disease) splits by LeRoy criteria into limited cutaneous disease (thickening distal to elbows and knees, plus face) and diffuse cutaneous disease (thickening proximal to elbows and knees, reaching chest, abdomen, or upper arms). The subset at presentation predicts antibodies, organs, and mortality together. Proximal spread indicates diffuse disease with early organ screening.

vis.alt: Clinical and capillaroscopy features aiding systemic sclerosis diagnosis and subtyping.
vis.caption: Skin extent with capillary changes separates limited from diffuse disease at the first visit. Subset indicates the antibody panel. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Classification needs 9 points with finger thickening past knuckles sufficient alone. Skin is staged from puffy edema through thickening to atrophy. The Rodnan score from 0 to 51 tracks the course. Rising scores indicate active fibrotic disease.
steps.tx: Nine points or more on the 2013 ACR EULAR scale classifies SSc, and finger thickening that crosses the knuckles contributes **9 points** single-handedly. Skin travels from early edematous **puffy fingers** through hidebound thickening into late **atrophy** (thin tethered skin), measured by the modified Rodnan skin score (**mRSS**, a 17-site thickness scale) spanning **0 to 51 points**. A climbing mRSS indicates active fibrotic disease needing immunosuppression.

steps.say: Diffuse disease is linked to Scl-70 and RNA polymerase 3 with rapid skin change and early organs. Limited disease is CREST with centromere antibodies and late lung vessel disease. The antibody panel at diagnosis is the predictor of the decade ahead.
steps.tx: Rapid skin spread with early organ hits marks diffuse SSc, home to anti-topoisomerase I (**Scl-70**) and anti-**RNA polymerase III** with the highest mortality. Slow distal disease is **CREST** (calcinosis, Raynaud, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia) carrying anti-**centromere** antibodies and late lone pulmonary arterial hypertension. Ordering all three antibodies at diagnosis predicts the decade ahead.

vis.alt: Diffuse systemic sclerosis with mask facies, skin thickening, ulcers, fibrosis, and organ involvement.
vis.caption: Mask facies with hidebound skin and ulcers mark diffuse disease with early organ risk. Antibodies confirm the subset. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: RNA polymerase 3 is the warning of renal crisis in up to 25 percent with synchronous cancer. Tendon friction rubs are the markers of the same patients. Blood pressure is watched at home. New hypertension with falling counts is crisis until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: Grating tendon **friction rubs** (creaking sheaths) with anti-**RNA polymerase III** forecast renal crisis in up to **25 percent** plus cancer arriving in the same window. Scleroderma **renal crisis** (malignant hypertension with microangiopathy) kills within days unless ACE inhibition starts, so home blood pressure logs are required. Fresh hypertension with dropping platelets indicates crisis, never essential hypertension.

vis.alt: Cortical renal infarcts with onion-skin vascular proliferation and blood schistocytes in renal crisis.
vis.caption: Onion-skin vessels with schistocytes mark renal crisis under the microscope. Home pressures catch it early. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Nailfold capillaries are the staging test of microvascular disease over time. Giant loops above 50 micrometers open the sequence with hemorrhages and dropout following. Ramified bushes close the sequence. Every Raynaud patient with positive ANA requires capillaroscopy.
steps.tx: Nailfold capillaroscopy stages microvascular injury: early giant loops above **50 micrometers**, active **microhemorrhages** (tiny bleeds), dropout with **avascular** areas (capillary deserts), and late ramified **neoangiogenesis** (bushy new vessels). The scleroderma pattern with Raynaud and positive ANA defines very early SSc, progressing to definite disease within 5 years in above 60 percent untreated. Capillaroscopy is required in every ANA positive Raynaud patient.

steps.say: CREST is the collection of calcinosis, Raynaud, dysmotility, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasia under centromere antibodies. Late pulmonary hypertension is the threat after years of calm skin. Annual echocardiography tracks pressures. Breathlessness in CREST is vascular until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: Limited SSc is **CREST**: calcinosis (calcium lumps), Raynaud phenomenon, esophageal **dysmotility** (weak swallowing), **sclerodactyly** (tapered tight fingers), and **telangiectasia** (matted red vessels), with anti-centromere antibodies. Late isolated pulmonary arterial hypertension threatens after years of calm skin. Annual echocardiography tracks pressures, because breathlessness in CREST is vascular until proven otherwise.

points: Diffuse skin with Scl-70 or Pol3
right.title: Diffuse SSc

steps.say: Sine scleroderma occurs without any skin thickening in below 5 percent. Organ failure occurs with positive antibodies and normal skin. Oesophageal, lung, pressure, and renal screens are still applied. Normal skin never excludes systemic sclerosis.
steps.tx: Systemic sclerosis **sine scleroderma** (organ disease without skin disease) affects below **5 percent**: full internal disease of esophagus, lung, pulmonary vessels, and kidney with SSc autoantibodies and zero cutaneous thickening. Dysphagia, fibrosis, hypertension, and crisis screens apply exactly as in diffuse disease. Normal skin with SSc antibodies and organ injury indicates sine disease, never reassurance.

steps.say: Subset, antibodies, skin score, capillaries, and pressures are the staging panel of every patient. Diffuse disease is watched for crisis and cancer while limited disease is watched for late vascular disease. The first visit sets the surveillance for years.
steps.tx: Every new SSc patient is staged by subset, antibodies, **mRSS 0 to 51**, capillaroscopy, and pressures. Diffuse disease with RNA polymerase III is watched for renal crisis up to **25 percent** with synchronous malignancy, while limited CREST is watched for late pulmonary hypertension. Digital ulcers in up to **50 percent** take bosentan cover. The first visit sets surveillance for the decade.
